This is impacting our SLAs — tagging our ops lead Tom Hwang and the platform team.

Thanks,

Quick triage notes (initial):

- No planned deployments or infra maintenance in the US region during 00:45–02:45 UTC. No autoscaler flapping seen in the cluster logs.
- We see a short burst of 5xxs originating from several frontends starting 2026-07-20T01:06:22Z. Latency increased concurrently.
- Correlation: multiple FinFlow worker hosts issued repeated requests with sub-50ms backoff/back-to-back retries (see extracted client patterns in the attached logs).
- Our serving layer experienced a transient queueing effect; because the client-side retries had effectively no exponential backoff, the retry volume saturated connection pools and pushed up p99 latency and 5xx surface area.

Immediate recommendations we pushed to FinFlow ops (attached patch):
1) Reduce client concurrency for batch workers to <= 8 per host for reconciliation runs.
2) Implement exponential backoff with jitter (recommended initial=100ms, multiplier=2, max=2s).
3) Temporarily enable per-account ingress rate limiting on your routes while you roll out the SDK/config change.

We’ve attached a small patch (sdk-backoff-config-diff.patch) with suggested default values and a sample migration note for their fleet. I’ll also prepare a short KB entry and doc change to call out our recommended retry semantics.

I’m leaving a thin mitigation in place: a conservative per-account soft-limit for the model endpoint that should prevent runaway retries from causing cluster-wide degradation. This limit is non-disruptive and can be increased once FinFlow’s client changes are deployed.

Marissa
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sdk-backoff-config-diff.patch

Date: 2026-07-21T13:42:00Z
Subject: RE: Intermittent 5xxs & retry amplification during batch jobs — follow up and remediation

Update after postmortem + remediation steps we executed:

- Cause: cascade driven by client-side retry configuration in FinFlow’s reconciliation workers. Defaults in an older internal SDK were aggressive (no jitter, very small initial delay). When a small number of requests hit transient 5xxs, the fleet retried en masse.
- Platform role: we did not have a pre-existing per-account soft ingress limit for that account; we now have a conservative soft-limit (requests/sec) in place to avoid cross-account blast radius. No infra deployment or bug on our side caused the initial 5xxs.

Actions completed:
1) Issued KB and SDK patch to FinFlow (recommended default: initial=100ms, multiplier=2, jitter=10-50%, max=2s). Patch attached.
2) Applied per-account soft ingress limit for FinFlow route (temporary, non-disruptive).
3) Added a defensive server-side queue cutoff so retries from a single source can’t occupy >20% of a worker’s connection pool.
4) Scheduled a platform change to make per-account soft-limits default for customers running >50 concurrent batch workers.
5) Drafted customer-facing incident summary and proposed a one-time goodwill credit; Connor to finalize credit amount with Finance.

We recommend FinFlow roll the SDK change to their fleet overnight and confirm reduced retry counts tomorrow morning (we’ll monitor).

Next steps:
- FinFlow to deploy SDK change (Sam/Tom).
- Redwood to monitor and revert soft-limit once traffic normalizes.
- Connor/Finance to confirm credit.

If FinFlow wants a joint postmortem doc for their compliance/audit team we can provide an annotated timeline and logs.

Marissa Cole
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
